== Biography ==
Mary Glasgow was a spinster living at Larne, County Antrim, when a marriage settlement was made on 10 February 1843 for her intended marriage to John McGavock of Larne, innkeeper. James Smyth of Larne, merchant, and Henry Magee of Curran, gentleman, were trustees. The deed records an intended marriage, not proof that the wedding took place on that date.<ref name="Settlement1843">Registry of Deeds, Ireland, memorial of marriage settlement, John McGavock and Mary Glasgow, dated 10 February 1843, affidavit 14 February, registered 18 February 1843; FamilySearch, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-FQ3Q opening image 499] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-F3BZ continuation image 500], original images inspected 21 September 2026. The complete book and memorial reference remains to be verified.</ref>

Mary settled an undivided half share of tenements on the north and south sides of Newtown Larne, together with a field and adjoining houses north of Pound Road. An endorsement concerned £250 to be paid to McGavock by the trustees or executors of the will of [[Glasgow-4180|Hugh Glasgow]], deceased. It does not state Hugh's relationship to Mary.<ref name="Settlement1843" />

=== Probable census identification ===
The 1851 census for house 1, Cross Street, Larne, records John McGavock, 50, widower, merchant and innkeeper, with marriage years 1824, 1827 and 1843. Its deceased-household table lists Mary McGavock, wife, aged 37, who died of jaundice in autumn 1843.<ref name="Census1851">National Archives of Ireland, 1851 census, County Antrim, Larne, Cross Street, house 1, John McGavock household; [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/view-pdf/?doc=007246521_00320&c19=true household and marriage table, image 007246521_00320] and [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/view-pdf/?doc=007246521_00321&c19=true absent and deceased household members, image 007246521_00321], original return inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

The husband's name, occupation, place and 1843 marriage make this a strong candidate for the settlement couple. The census gives no maiden surname for the deceased wife, so the identification remains provisional. The estimated birth about 1806, uncertain death in 1843 and married name McGavock on this profile depend on that identification. The two absent sons James and John, aged 22, predate the 1843 marriage and have not been assigned to Mary.<ref name="Census1851" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Uncertain father ===
[[Glasgow-4180|Hugh Glasgow]], the deceased testator, is attached as Mary's '''uncertain father'''. A father's provision for a daughter's marriage is a coherent working explanation for the estate payment, but no father-daughter wording appears in the inspected deed. He could have been another relative or benefactor. His own proposed attachment to [[Glasgow-3991|James Glasgow]] is a separate low-confidence hypothesis, not evidence establishing Mary's parentage.<ref name="Settlement1843" />

=== Possible duplicate: Mary Glasgow-3989 ===
[[Glasgow-3989|Mary Glasgow]], daughter of [[Glasgow-3324|William Glasgow]], remains a possible identity for the bride. The Larne monument names her father and records her death on '''18 October 1844 aged 37''', conflicting with the probable census wife's death in '''autumn 1843 aged 37'''.<ref>"Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim," ''Ulster Journal of Archaeology'', second series, volume 6 (1900), [https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up p. 47], William Glasgow family monument transcription.</ref> Separate profiles are retained provisionally; they are not evidence that two women have been proved. Resolve this through the marriage or burial register, original stone and property-title succession before merging. If they are the same person, William's monument-proved fatherhood takes precedence and the proposed Hugh-father link must be withdrawn.

=== Inferred locations ===
Larne is Mary's recorded residence in the settlement, not a proved birthplace. It is entered as an uncertain birth location from that context. The uncertain death location is inferred from the probable Cross Street household, not an explicit place-of-death statement.<ref name="Settlement1843" /><ref name="Census1851" />
